title: Tenant network operational contract and event stream (PRD draft)
body:
Context:
We need a lightweight PRD that defines the operational contract between Redwood and customers for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. The focus here is two-fold: (1) a small, well-defined event stream / audit ingestion schema that captures the lifecycle of a tenant network change and (2) a concise contract that specifies expectations, SLAs, and required evidence for approvals and rollbacks. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — MVP first, richer features (deep attestation, cryptographic receipts) later.

Goals (MVP):
- Define a minimal event schema that covers change initiation, approval, application, verification, and rollback.
- Specify retention, indexing keys, and sampling policies so logs are useful for post-incident forensics and automated SLO checks.
- Draft an operational contract (customer <> Redwood) with clear triggers for escalation, required proof artifacts, and acceptable latency for audit ingestion.
- Provide example flows for manual-approved, automated-approved, and emergency rollbacks.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full PKI-based attestation (future scope).
- Deep telemetry of device internals (beyond what the customer supplies).
- On-prem UI for browsing raw audit streams (we'll expose via API/dashboards later).

Event model (flat, short names — for efficient streaming):
Event fields (all strings unless noted):
- event_id: unique uuid
- tenant_id: tenant GUID
- change_id: tenant-local id for the change bundle
- event_type: one of [CHANGE_INITIATED, APPROVAL_REQUESTED, APPROVAL_DECISION, CONFIG_APPLIED, VERIFY_PASS, VERIFY_FAIL, AUDIT_SNAPSHOT, ROLLBACK_INITIATED, ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, ERROR_SAMPLE]
- source: origin of event (operator-console | api | operator-agent | customer-webhook)
- actor: short name or service (ops:alice, cust:netops-team)
- timestamp_iso: RFC3339
- summary: short human-readable summary (<=200 chars)
- details_url: optional URL to stored diff, snapshot, or log bundle (signed link)
- proof_id: optional id for evidence bundle (e.g., snapshot GUID)

Example: 
{"event_id":"e3c1...","tenant_id":"t-42","change_id":"chg-2024-09-12-7","event_type":"CHANGE_INITIATED","source":"operator-console","actor":"ops:alice","timestamp_iso":"2024-09-12T14:12:09Z","summary":"BGP peer update planned","details_url":"https://s3.redwood/.../chg-2024-09-12-7/diff.json","proof_id":"pf-99"}

Operational contract (high level):
- Ingestion SLA: Redwood will persist and acknowledge audit events within 10s (99th pct) once events are received by the control-plane API. If customer uses a push model (webhook -> Redwood), delivery SLA is defined separately.
- Evidence required for approval gates: approval decision events MUST include details_url pointing to the approval bundle (signed by approver identity if possible). For automated approvals, attached rule_id and evaluation snapshot are required.
- Immutable ledger behavior: events are append-only in our ingestion store. Customers will get a cryptographic digest artifact on request (future scope). For MVP we log event_id, timestamp, and details_url and keep retention metadata.

Retention & indexing policy (MVP):
- Full event retention: 365 days for standard Private customers, configurable up to 7 years via enterprise add-on.
- Hot indexing: index by tenant_id, change_id, event_type, actor for fast queries (to support triangle queries like "what approvals exist for change X").
- Sample retention: store full details only for 100% of APPROVAL_DECISION and CONFIG_APPLIED events. For high-volume ERROR_SAMPLE events, store metadata + 1:10 sampled details.

Verification & cross-checks:
- Verify event arrival ordering by change_id/timestamp; if out-of-order, tag event with ordering_warning and surface in console.
- Cross-validate CONFIG_APPLIED with a periodic AUDIT_SNAPSHOT (e.g., device-config hash). If verification fails, emit VERIFY_FAIL and auto-create ROLLBACK_INITIATED if policy demands.

Approval gates (policy options):
1) Manual-Only: any change requires APPROVAL_DECISION with approver identity and details_url.
2) Rule-Based: automated rules (e.g., minor ACL edits <10 lines) can be allowed; decisions must include rule_id and evaluation snapshot.
3) Escalation: if approval not provided within T_window (configurable), route to emergency on-call and NR.

Customer responsibilities (summary):
- Provide a webhook endpoint or agent for event push, or use Redwood-managed control-plane API to submit events.
- Keep approver identities up to date in-provisioning (for audit binding).
- Retain local configs as canonical sources for deep forensics; Redwood's event stream is an operational index, not the primary archive for full device state.

Admin UX notes (quick):
- Quick search: by change_id, tenant_id, event_type — support freeform time ranges.
- Timeline view: render events grouped by change_id with color-coding for decisions, apply, verify, rollback.
- Download evidence: single-click bundle containing details_url artifacts (signed at time of ingestion if provided).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Ingestion API endpoint documented + Postman/SDK example.
- Storage of events with metadata searchable by tenant_id and change_id.
- Approval gate enforcement for Manual-Only policy on a per-tenant config.
- Example demo: simulate a network change from initiation -> manual approval -> apply -> verification -> pass.

Open questions / risks (action items):
- Do we require signed approver tokens at MVP? (tradeoff: integration friction vs stronger guarantees). TODO: prod-privacy to weigh in. @Jia
- Storage cost estimates for full retention (365d) at expected Private deployment event rate. Action: infra to provide cost model. @Ethan
- How to surface out-of-order ingestion to SRE vs product dashboards (noise risk). Proposal: only surface for >1% of events.

Future scope:
- Cryptographic receipts (signed digests at ingestion time) and customer-verifiable ledger export.
- Deep attestation integrations (HSM/KMS-proof that device applied config) with vendor adapters.
- Metrics-driven risk scoring for changes (auto-highlighting risky changes).

Next steps (short):
- Iterate with infra on schema size and ingestion latency (1 week).
- Build a stub ingestion API + sample client for customer agents (2 sprints).
- Demo run with 2 pilot customers and refine retention/sampling config (Q4).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally trimmed to operational essentials. I'm trying to avoid doubling down on attestation primitives in the MVP. Please call out any mandatory evidence you think we must require from the start.
- If we agree on schema, I'll add a compact OpenAPI contract and lightweight JSON Schema for event validation.

---
Checklist (quick TODOs):
- [ ] confirm ingestion latency target with infra
- [ ] cost model for 365d retention at 10k events/day/tenant
- [ ] sample client code + Postman collection
- [ ] run a tabletop with solutions-eng to validate example flows
